name: BICEP2
notes: The 2014 detection claim was withdrawn by the later joint analysis: "We find strong evidence for dust and no statistically significant evidence for tensor modes" (arXiv:1502.00612). Both results are recorded as separate result records.

physics_goals.quote: BICEP2 experiment, a cosmic microwave background (CMB) polarimeter specifically designed to search for the signal of inflationary gravitational waves in the B-mode power spectrum around $\ell\sim80$.
physics_goals.value: Search for the B-mode signal of inflationary gravitational waves around multipole l ~ 80.

summary.plain: A 26-centimetre telescope at the South Pole that watched one patch of sky for three seasons. In 2014 it reported an excess of polarization attributed to gravitational waves, which a joint analysis with Planck data then traced largely to dust.
summary.technical: CMB polarimeter at the South Pole (Dark Sector Laboratory), 512 TES bolometers at 150 GHz, 2010-2012, ~400 deg^2; reported a B-mode excess at 30 < l < 150 (BICEP2 I, 2014) that BICEP2/Keck/Planck (2015) found consistent with dust; successor to BICEP1 and basis of the Keck Array and BICEP3 data.
